title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's 'Programme de la théorie de Dieudonné sur une base S où p est localement nilpotent'. Earlier pages built a contravariant crystalline Dieudonné functor D*: BT(S)^o → Crisloclib(S), with values in locally free crystals. It is compatible with base change and depends only on G_0 = G ×_S S_0, where S_0 = V(p). In characteristic p the Frobenius and Verschiebung of G induce maps F_M: M^(p) → M and V_M: M → M^(p) with VF = p and FV = p. This makes M = D*(G_0) an F-V-crystal (Dieudonné crystal). Over a perfect field the functor recovers classical Dieudonné theory, which is an (anti-)equivalence.

The page draws the consequence. For a general base S_0 of characteristic p, the F-V-crystal M determines all geometric fibres G_{0,s̄} over perfect fields. So M 'essentially captures' the family.

Grothendieck then states Problem 1, which he says he has not solved. Is the Dieudonné functor fully faithful over an arbitrary characteristic-p base S_0? Is its essential image the class of 'admissible' F-V-crystals defined later?

His proposed strategy is to build a Dieudonné theory for arbitrary finite locally free p-group schemes over S_0, or at least those flat over Λ_n = Z/p^n. This would be an equivalence with F-V-crystals equipped with extra structure he has not yet isolated. He expects that structure to involve a suitable filtration on an object of a derived category.

A marginal pencil note says this extra structure is 'sans doute inutile si S_0 est parfait'. This leads to Problem 2 on the next page: over perfect S_0, an anti-equivalence between finite locally free groups flat over Λ_n and locally free W_n(O_S)-modules with F and V.
errors: No mathematical error. Full faithfulness over arbitrary characteristic-p bases is not a general theorem today. It is known under hypotheses: Berthelot–Breen–Messing for bases with local p-bases, de Jong for formally smooth and related bases, and later results over perfect, semiperfect and some other rings. So Grothendieck rightly left it open.
The claim that M recovers the fibres at perfect points relies on compatibility with base change plus the classical theorem over perfect fields. This is correct as stated.

ideas.what: Crystalline Dieudonné functor from BT groups to F-V-crystals over a characteristic-p base, compatible with base change, recovering classical theory over perfect fields
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory / Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux, Actes ICM Nice 1970; Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Presses Univ. Montréal, 1974)

ideas.what: Problem 1: full faithfulness of the Dieudonné functor over a characteristic-p base, and its essential image being the 'admissible' F-V-crystals
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness / essential image of the crystalline Dieudonné functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Posed by Grothendieck (ICM 1970). Partial solutions: Berthelot–Messing, de Jong (1995), Lau, Scholze–Weinstein, Anschütz–Le Bras (semiperfect/quasisyntomic)
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 report and Montréal notes list these problems

ideas.what: Strategy: extend Dieudonné theory to finite locally free p-group schemes via F-V-crystals with extra structure, probably a filtration on an object of a derived category
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné crystals of finite flat group schemes (BBM). Filtered/derived Dieudonné theory: Illusie's deformation theory via the cotangent complex, Fontaine–Laffaille and Breuil–Kisin filtrations, prismatic Dieudonné theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Breen–Messing; Illusie 1985; Breuil, Kisin; Anschütz–Le Bras; Bhatt–Lurie
ideas.where_published: The idea of extending to finite groups is in the Montréal notes. The specific 'filtration on an object of a derived category' phrasing is unsure.

ideas.what: Marginal remark that no extra structure is needed over perfect bases
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné theory over perfect rings (finite flat group schemes ↔ W_n-modules with F, V)
ideas.where_published: Problem 2 of the ICM 1970 report / Montréal notes

missed.claim: Grothendieck expected the missing structure classifying finite flat group schemes over general characteristic-p bases to be a filtration on an object of a derived category. This anticipates filtered or derived approaches: Illusie's use of the cotangent complex and later prismatic/derived Dieudonné theories with Hodge-type filtrations. It appears only as a vague remark, and the phrasing may already be in the circulated Montréal notes.
missed.quote: très probablement impliqueront la donnée d'une filtration convenable sur un objet d'une catégorie dérivée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor of derived/filtered Dieudonné theory (e.g. Anschütz–Le Bras, Bhatt–Lurie). It is of minor interest since the programme has since been carried out by other means.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of material essentially published in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 report and Montréal notes, where Problems 1 and 2 appear. The only mildly notable detail is the explicit 'filtration on an object of a derived category' heuristic and the pencil remark about perfect bases.
transcription_corrections: 'réconstituer' is indeed typed with the accent (Grothendieck's typo), so the transcription is faithful.
The marginal note near 'importante' reads 'en ce sens' (handwritten above, inserted before 'que je').
The pencil note at the bottom right reads 'sans doute inutile si S_o est parfait' and is linked by a line to the circled 'muni de structures supplémentaires (*)'.
'G_{o s̄}' is G_0 subscript with s-bar (geometric points).
